lines.text: Open in London first, then New York and Atlanta: that is where your comps' audience is strongest among your cities.
Keep your target of people aged 25 to 34, but lead the creative with people 45 to 54, then 24 and under, leaning male, where these comps are strongest.
Attach the trailer to Extraction II and The Equalizer 3.
Push the idea of a heist that escalates fast and cannot be walked back, because heist is the clearest topic that separates this lane from other recent crime-thriller releases.
Pitch the film to buyers and press in the company of Widows, a title you named.
Pitch the film to buyers and press in the company of Baby Driver, a title you named.
In London, the strongest people for this title are concentrated in Peckham and Brixton, so street teams and creator capture should be built around those neighborhoods first.
London should follow immediately after New York, with BFI IMAX and Curzon Mayfair for premium positioning and The Clapham Grand for event energy; build the local push around Peckham and Brixton.
Plan Atlanta as a smaller market: focus on diaspora community screenings rather than a wide booking.
Manchester ranks above Atlanta for this audience. Weigh it beside your cities, not instead of them.
The audience data says people like this are there. It does not say the market will sell, so check how you would reach them in Manchester before you move any of your plan.
Run one small test in Manchester: the creative you already have, on your lead channel, with a fixed budget, before you change anything else.
Judge it on Advance screenings and presales in Manchester, against Atlanta.
In London, the audience is strongest around Peckham and Brixton.
This is a lead from a few points near the centre of London, not a measured neighbourhood. Walk it or ask someone local before you book anything.
Put one small activation in Peckham, such as a screening, a signing, a listening event or flyers with a local venue, and note who turns up.
Judge it on Advance screenings and presales from Peckham, against London as a whole.
In New York, the audience is strongest around Harlem and Brooklyn.
This is a lead from a few points near the centre of New York, not a measured neighbourhood. Walk it or ask someone local before you book anything.
Put one small activation in Harlem, such as a screening, a signing, a listening event or flyers with a local venue, and note who turns up.
Judge it on Advance screenings and presales from Harlem, against New York as a whole.
In Atlanta, the audience is strongest around Midtown and Downtown.
This is a lead from a few points near the centre of Atlanta, not a measured neighbourhood. Walk it or ask someone local before you book anything.
Put one small activation in Midtown, such as a screening, a signing, a listening event or flyers with a local venue, and note who turns up.
Judge it on Advance screenings and presales from Midtown, against Atlanta as a whole.

Attach the trailer and paid social cutdowns to Extraction II, The Equalizer 3 and The Covenant where inventory is available, because those recent action-crime titles sit closest to the audience already showing up for this lane.
Use crime-thriller and R-rated adjacent placements rather than broad family inventory, because the strongest audience signal comes from adult crime, thriller and action behavior.
If a cinema buy is available, prioritize adult-oriented screens and late-night showtimes in the three launch cities, then use the same spots for trailer runs and local paid social cutdowns.

Book true-crime and crime-story podcasts in Atlanta first, especially My Favorite Murder with Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark, Last Podcast On The Left and To Live and Die in LA, and give them a straight heist-pressure angle rather than a plot recap.
names: My Favorite Murder with Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark
To Live and Die in LA

lines.text: For creators, use crime, sneaker, car-culture and late-night film-talk creators rather than general lifestyle pages; give them short clips, one heist-pressure line and one city-specific hook cut for Atlanta, New York and London.

Cut vertical teaser clips and reaction-ready snippets for paid social and creator reposts, with Atlanta versions leading on local pride, New York on urgency and London on premium crime-thriller style.

In Atlanta, pair one community screening or meet-up with Patchwerk Recording Studios or The Crown Room, because those event spaces and music-adjacent rooms are the cleanest fit for a launch-night crowd.

In New York, use NYFA, Columbia and Manhattan University for student and alumni turnout, then anchor one screening or cast-free panel around Social Drink & Food or Color Factory NYC if you need a social-space event.
names: NYFA I New York Film Academy
Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons

lines.text: In London, work with King's College London, the University of Greenwich and the London Film School, then use Central Hall Westminster or the Queen Elizabeth II Centre for one larger discussion-led event.
Use churches and associations only where a local leader already runs film nights or men’s groups, because the ask should be turnout and introductions, not a sermon pitch.

Open Atlanta first, then New York and London within the same week or the next few days, because the film is U.S.-set, the home market should lead, and the tighter cadence reduces spoiler and piracy drag.
Plan a four-month run that starts with trailer, key art and partner asks now, moves into a six-to-eight week local build, then opens city by city with the Atlanta premiere as the first public moment.
Hold back the strongest clips, creator reactions and any premium stills for the week before each local opening so the campaign stays fresh across all three cities.
If the team wants a distributor route, keep the theatrical booking aligned to a voluntary rating submission for the U.S. release and a straight indie rollout through city-by-city bookings.
Home market. Lead on YouTube, Instagram and TikTok.
Lead on YouTube, Instagram and TikTok.
Lead on YouTube, Instagram and TikTok.
Lead the Atlanta cut with three hook options: a bank job gone sideways, a no-way-out heist pressure line, and a fast crime-thriller cut that plays like adult action rather than young swagger.
For New York, sharpen the hook around consequence and control slipping away, since the strongest audience is in Harlem and Brooklyn and responds to serious adult crime language.
For London, make the cut feel premium and tense, with the cleanest possible crime-thriller image and less flash than the heist-forward Atlanta version.
The key art should show a tense adult crime moment with banking, money movement or getaway cues, and it should avoid glossy youth styling, comedy cues or anything that makes it feel like a caper.
This calendar follows blog-level guidance, one source for each point. Treat it as direction, not a measured result.

Put about 80 percent of paid spend behind creative that has already worked, and about 20 percent into testing new creative.
Run three to five ads in each ad group.
Judge a winner by its conversion count, not by how many days it has run.
T-26 to T-16: Lock the title treatment and key art, cut the first teaser and set up the sales and presale page.
T-20 to T-12: Use a festival or market slot to build early press and distributor interest, never as the only beat.
T-12: Release the first trailer on the lead video platform and open advance screening sign-ups.

T-4 to T-3: Send the press screener and the second trailer, and confirm premiere guests.
T-1: Hold the home-market premiere, with the other territories following within days.
Launch week: Release and report advance screenings and presales to the team daily.
T+1 to T+4: Move spend to the territories where presales and screenings are ahead, and plan the streaming or home release window.
A starting split of $40,000: adjust it with your distributor, and move money first to the cities with the strongest pre-sales.
Paid media and trailer placement: 40%, $16,000.
Publicity and press: 15%, $6,000.
Community screenings and events: 15%, $6,000.
Creative (trailer, key art, cut-downs): 15%, $6,000.
Partnerships and tie-ins: 5%, $2,000.
Contingency: 10%, $4,000.
Judge this plan on one signal: advance screenings and presales.
No target is set. Give your own number, such as “target 10,000”, and the plan will carry it.
Read it 56, 28 and 7 days before release.
Trailer views, Followers, Press mentions are secondary: track them, but do not judge the plan on them.

The main taste risk is that the comp audience skews older than men 25 to 34, so the fix is to keep the target but write the ads in adult crime language and book the strongest screens where the audience is densest.
Another risk is over-reading Baby Driver and pushing the campaign too young or too playful; keep the crime and consequence front and center so the film still feels serious to the older male crowd.

Atlanta is the smallest of the three comp cities, so it should stay the launch anchor but not absorb the whole budget; use it for premiere energy and community turnout, then let New York and London carry more of the reach.
If paid media starts to drift broad, pull it back into the top screens, creator clips and neighborhood work rather than trying to buy every audience at once.

criteria.text: Provides a strategy tailored to a budget of around forty thousand dollars
Outlines marketing tactics specifically for men aged twenty-five to thirty-four in Atlanta, New York, and London
Aligns the release timing with a four-month window
Reflects the tone and audience tastes established by Widows and Baby Driver

issues.text: The budget split gives a full $40k plan, but it is not actually tailored to the budget in a defendable way: several line items are generic, and the plan never explains why the spend should be tilted toward London/New York despite Atlanta being the launch city the person named.
issues.fix: Rework the budget into a city-by-city allocation with a clear reason for each spend bucket, and show how the $40k is enough to cover the specific launch beats in Atlanta, New York, and London.

issues.text: The draft says to lead the creative with people 45 to 54 and 24 and under, which conflicts with the user’s stated target of men aged 25 to 34. That audience guidance also turns the requested targeting into a secondary buy instead of the campaign focus.
issues.fix: Keep men 25 to 34 as the primary audience in voice, placements, and creative direction, while using the comp audience insight only as a support signal for channel choice or messaging angles.

issues.text: The release route and timeline are not aligned with the stated four-month window. The draft introduces a long prelude (T-26 to T-16) and a post-theatrical arc that reads like a much longer rollout than the requested about-four-month launch plan.
issues.fix: Condense the plan into a four-month calendar from now to release, with concrete milestones for announcement, trailer, screenings, press, and opening week in that window.

issues.text: The comp framing is treated as settled, but the evidence says the comps lean older and only one title is doing much of the work. The draft repeats Widows and Baby Driver as if the fit is confirmed, without softening that to a tentative positioning choice.
issues.fix: Present Widows and Baby Driver as reference points, but hedge the claim that they fully define the audience fit and say the campaign should borrow their heist/crime energy rather than assume they are the exact audience match.

issues.text: The draft changes the requested opening order to London first, then New York and Atlanta. The person asked to open in Atlanta, New York and London, so this directly ignores the city order they gave.
issues.fix: Restore the launch order to Atlanta, New York, then London, or explicitly frame any alternative order as a recommendation that the person must approve.

issues.text: The plan pushes the heaviest spend and effort into London and New York because the comp audience is stronger there, which sidelines Atlanta even though the user asked to open there.
issues.fix: Keep Atlanta as one of the opening markets and make the plan reflect the requested three-city launch, even if London is the strongest taste match.

issues.text: The budget section does use the $40,000 figure, but the plan repeatedly tells the team to ‘adjust it with your distributor’ and to move money toward the strongest pre-sales, which drifts from the user’s fixed around-$40k launch budget into a distributor-led spend model.
issues.fix: Keep the $40k allocation as the governing constraint and present the split as the working plan, with only small rebalancing notes that still stay within that total.

issues.text: The draft still centers the campaign on people 45 to 54 and 24 and under, then says the target of men 25 to 34 should only guide media buying. That directly conflicts with the user’s stated primary audience.
issues.fix: Make men aged 25 to 34 the lead audience for creative, media, and partnerships, and treat the older skew as a secondary insight rather than the campaign’s core.

issues.text: The release route says to open in London first, then New York and Atlanta, and the timeline says the home market premiere comes first. The user asked to open in Atlanta, New York and London, so the sequence is wrong in two places.
issues.fix: Restore the opening order to Atlanta, then New York, then London, and align the timeline and release route to that sequence.

issues.text: The draft treats Widows and Baby Driver as settled positioning anchors, but the evidence says the comp fit leans on one title and skews older than the user’s target. The wording is too certain for the support available.
issues.fix: Soften the comp framing: present Widows and Baby Driver as reference points for tone and market language, while signaling that the core audience insight comes from the crime-thriller lane and adjacent audience behavior, not a fully confirmed comp match.

issues.text: The plan says to keep the 25–34 target but lead the creative with people 45–54 and 24 and under, which reverses the user’s stated primary audience of men 25–34.
issues.fix: Make men 25–34 the lead audience in the creative, media, and channel plan; use any older or younger audience insight only as a secondary testing note, not the campaign lead.

issues.text: The release route opens London first and then New York and Atlanta, and the timeline also puts the home-market premiere first. The user asked to open in Atlanta, New York, and London.
issues.fix: Rewrite the launch sequence to start in Atlanta, then New York, then London, while keeping the four-month window intact.

issues.text: Widows and Baby Driver are treated as firm positioning anchors, but the evidence says the comps lean older and only one title is doing much of the work. The draft sounds more certain about the fit than the data supports.
issues.fix: Soften the comp language to a tentative positioning choice and anchor the campaign more clearly in the proven crime/thriller, heist, and car-chase signals instead of presenting the comps as fully settled.

next: Tighten the budget plan so each line shows what gets bought in Atlanta, New York, and London for roughly $40k.
Turn the timeline into city-by-city dates relative to release, using the four-month window as the backbone.
Add one more comp or a clearer story/cast hook so the positioning is less dependent on Widows and Baby Driver.
